questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

____ woman in ____ picture is my mother.
questions.solution_en:
The most appropriate option to fill in the blanks is (a). The article "the" is used before "woman" to refer to a specific woman, indicating that the speaker is talking about a particular woman known to the speaker. Using 'a' before 'woman' suggests any woman rather than a specific one, which doesn't align with the context that refers to a particular woman (speaker's mother) known to the speaker. 'An' is the indefinite article used before words that begin with a vowel sound. However, "woman" starts with a consonant sound. So, "an" is not appropriate here.

The article "the" is also used before "picture" because it is a specific picture known to both the speaker and the listener. The speaker is talking about a specific picture of his/her mother. Using "a" before 'picture' suggests any picture rather than a specific one. So, "a" is not suitable in this case. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

A noun is a word used as the name of a person, place, or thing. Now consider the following sentences:

1) Mahesh is a clever boy.

2) A herd of cattle was grazing on the pastureland.

3) Honesty is the best policy.

An article is a word that comes before a noun to indicate whether it's specific or general.

Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The tragedies of the past ____ us that hegemony and group politics bring no peace or security.
questions.solution_en:
The sentence conveys that group politics and hegemony do not bring peace. Option (c) is eliminated because it is a present participle verb and a present participle verb requires a helping verb such as "is/am/are/been" to precede it. The subject of the sentence is 'tragedies' which is plural in nature. According to subject-verb agreement, we cannot use a singular verb with a plural subject. So, options (a) and (d) are eliminated because those are singular verbs (third person singular). The plural verb 'tell' is the correct choice here. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

Note:-

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

questions.q_en:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. The aviation industry's energy-related CO2 emissions have grown faster than those of rail, road and shipping in recent decades, according to the International Energy Agency.

B. To understand the potential impact of switching from traditional jet fuel to hydrogen fuel in aviation, Anna Cybulsky, Mallapragada and colleagues modelled its use in the electrification of regional and short-range turboprop aircraft.

C. Hydrogen's appeal as a fuel source is that its use produces no CO2 and provides more energy per pound than jet fuel.

D. To reduce the potential climate impacts of this growth, scientists are improving aircraft design and operation, and developing low-emission fuels such as hydrogen, which is used for direct combustion or to power electric fuel cells.
questions.solution_en:
If the sentences are read carefully, it can be noted that sentence A describes the premise of the discussion by stating the problem that is discussed through the sentences. So, sentence A comes first in the sequence.

It is followed by sentence D, which talks about the alternative in the trial for jet fuel. This context is contradicted in sentence C, in which the actual condition of hydrogen fuel for the jet engine is stated. So, it comes third in the order.

Sentence B concludes the passage by stating what needs to be done and what research has been going on, regarding hydrogen fuels. So, the final order is ADCB.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

In the part of Italy that is known as Umbria, there stands the little town of Assisi, built on the slopes of Monte Subasio. Assisi is a very old city - some say it dates as far back as 400 or 500 B.C. - and underneath its streets are long passages that come out far away in the hills, as if the citizens had used them in times of siege as a means of escape. If you studied its ruins of temples, theatres, and circuses, you would learn a great deal of history, not only of Assisi itself but of Rome as well. Totila, the Goth, halted there for a short time on his way to besiege the Eternal City. Charlemagne passed through it two hundred and fifty years later; while in the struggle for power between the pope and the emperor during the Middle Ages, the town sided first with one and then with the other. But, against one enemy, the people of Assisi never ceased fighting, and that was with the citizens of Perugia, which lay across the hills and could be seen plainly from the castle on the top. Among all the merchants of Assisi, none was so rich or well thought of as Bernadone, who carried on with France a large trade in silk and embroidered stuff. He had an only son, Giovanni, or John, born in 1182, and, as soon as the child was four or five years old, he had been taught French, so that by and by his father might send him across the sea to sell his goods to the noble ladies of the French court, and as no one in Assisi ever thought of learning any language but Italian, the boy was nicknamed "Il Francesco," or "the Frenchman." This nickname would become symbolic of a remarkable future. Giovanni would grow up to transform not only his own life but also the lives of countless others, embodying values of humility and compassion that continue to resonate around the world.

(a) reducing our reliance on fossil fuels,

(b) investing in renewable energy sources

(c) and fostering sustainable economic growth

(d) like solar and wind power

(d) like solar and wind power - This phrase provides examples of "renewable energy sources," clarifying the subject. It naturally follows (b). So far: "Investing in renewable energy sources like solar and wind power"

(e) is crucial for mitigating climate change, - This is the predicate of the sentence, with "is crucial" being the verb phrase and "for mitigating climate change" explaining the primary importance or purpose. It follows (d): "...is crucial for mitigating climate change,"

(c) and fostering sustainable economic growth - This phrase, beginning with "and," introduces the third parallel outcome/purpose, completing the list of benefits.

Final sentence: "Investing in renewable energy sources like solar and wind power is crucial for mitigating climate change, reducing our reliance on fossil fuels, and fostering sustainable economic growth."

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

Select the option that expresses the given sentence in present perfect tense.

A) I had visited Paris several times in the past.

B) I visited Paris several times in the past.

C) I was visiting Paris several times in the past.

D) I have visited Paris several times in the past.
questions.solution_en:
The option that expresses the given sentence in present perfect tense is (d). The present perfect tense is used to indicate an action that was completed at an unspecified time in the past with a connection to the present. It is formed by using the following construct - "has/have + the past participle form (V3) of the main verb" (have visited). Only sentence D follows the correct structure of the present perfect tense. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

Note:

Directions [Set of 4 Questions]: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

The scenic hill town of Darjeeling is famous for its 3T's - Tea, Timber, and Tourists. Originally established as a British sanatorium, it quickly earned the nickname 'Queen of Hills' and has become a popular tourist spot. The charming town welcomes visitors with stunning landscapes, drifting clouds, and pleasant weather. However, the other side of this hill station is marked by the struggles of Darjeeling's residents, who face challenges with basic water and sanitation services. Darjeeling has become synonymous with water scarcity, still depending on the water supply system set up by the British government between 1910 and 1915 for just 10,000 residents. However, the city's current population is around 118,805. This unexpected growth has posed a major challenge in the proper planning and installation of crucial municipal services like water and sewage systems. The city presents a dual effect, offering increased options for accommodating tourists, while also raising concerns about the capacity of the city to absorb this rampant growth and the pressure it exerts on municipal services. Darjeeling is located on a landscape with uneven layers, leading most homes to depend on stacked stairs and narrow, slippery paths for access. The electric wires and water pipelines are intertwined, demonstrating a harmonious coexistence that highlights a symbiotic relationship between fire and water elements. In Darjeeling, people usually throw household waste into the jhoras (drains going down the hill). Jhoras are local stormwater drains or flood harvesting systems that play a vital role in managing excess water during storms. Similar to the Aahar Pynes in Bihar and Nullahs in the northern regions, these systems help to prevent flooding and protect the local environment. This drain, among others, leads to one of the most visited sites, RockVille Garden, a picturesque tourist location known for its natural waterfall. The mismanaged disposal of waste has further exacerbated the problem of solid waste, creating a mountain of waste amid the scenic Eastern Himalayan mountain range.

questions.q_en:
Spot the erroneous part if any, in the following sentence.

The professor and/ the researcher has(A)/ already/ left the(B)/ conference/ to attend an(C)/ important seminar. / No error (D).
questions.solution_en:
When two singular nouns are joined by 'and' and the definite article is placed before each noun, then that refers to different persons or things. This means the sentence has a plural subject. So, 'has' (singular verb) should be replaced by 'have' (plural verb) in the given sentence as the verb must agree with the subject. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

The final correct sentence would be: The professor and the researcher have already left the conference to attend an important seminar.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The prevention curriculum, called raising healthy children, was created by UW social work professors.
options_en: UW social work professors were created the prevention curriculum, called raising healthy children.
UW social work professors create the prevention curriculum, called raising healthy children.
UW social work professors created the prevention curriculum, called raising healthy children.
UW social work professors have created the prevention curriculum, called raising healthy children.
questions.solution_en:
The correct answer is option c).

The subject of the passive voice is changed into the object of the active voice. Also, the object of the passive voice is changed into the subject of the active voice.

The removal of the helping verb [was] and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from passive to active. The tense [simple past tense] does not change.

Passive voice- subject + was/were + V3+ by + object

Active voice- new subject + second form of the verb + new object

Hence, the correct active voice of the given sentence is “UW social work professors created the prevention curriculum, called raising healthy children.”
